cold_open.hook: AMD just tanked 7.5% while Adobe soared 5.5%—the AI trade is officially splitting into winners and wreckage.

markets.macro_note: Broad market flat, but AI narrative fracturing—chip stocks bleeding while software rallies on earnings optimism.

big_story.story_title: Tech stocks today: Big Tech earnings this week mark a pivotal moment for the AI trade
big_story.angle: The AI trade isn't one trade anymore—it's a Venn diagram of who can actually monetize it vs. who's just burning capex. This week's earnings will expose which camp each mega-cap is really in.

quick_hits.angle: CXMT's 466% debut is pure China-listing theater: a chipmaker nobody's heard of becomes the most valuable China-listed company in hours. The float is probably the size of a postage stamp.
Cocoa prices are down 40% from peak but chocolate bars still cost $7—retailers are pocketing the margin windfall instead of passing it through. Inflation theater.
Meta's smart glasses rollout is a masterclass in how NOT to launch hardware: limited supply, no killer app, and the company's own AI team seems more interested in chatbots than AR.
The UK is considering shutting down Jodrell Bank, one of the world's oldest radio telescopes, to save money. It's like selling your telescope to pay for a telescope.

odd_thing.joke_angle: A movie called 'Champagne and Bullets' is being ranked on the Mount Rushmore of bad films—which means someone watched it, took notes, and decided it deserved a historical monument.

yesterday_callback.topic: Oil at $100 is the tariff tax on everything else—shipping costs, manufacturing, inflation creep.
yesterday_callback.fresh_take: Cocoa prices are down but chocolate is still expensive: retailers are hoarding the margin instead of passing savings through. Same playbook as tariff pass-through—companies test how much consumers will tolerate before they actually cut prices.

sign_off.callback_target: AMD's 7.5% drop—the chip sector's canary in the coal mine for whether AI capex is actually paying off or just burning cash.
